... SECOND INNINGS ...

Justin Greaves, the star of the innings, remained unbeaten on 115, registering his maiden Test century in an innings marked by patience and skill. Kemar Roach also contributed a vital 47 runs before falling to Mahmud, who finished as Bangladesh's standout bowler with figures of 3/87. The declaration came shortly after Greaves reached his century, signaling the end of a grueling effort by the hosts. Bangladesh will now face the challenge of responding to a daunting total. Their innings will begin shortly, with the Windies bowlers eager to capitalize on the scoreboard pressure. Stay tuned as the action continues!

After being invited to bat first by Bangladesh, the Windies overcame early setbacks with composed partnerships in the middle order. Mikyle Louis (97) and Alick Athanaze (90) were pivotal on Day 1, stitching together a 140-run stand for the fourth wicket. Both batters came agonizingly close to their centuries but fell in the nervous nineties, missing out on what could have been landmark knocks. Day 2 saw the home side continue their momentum. Although Hasan Mahmud struck early in the morning session, a sensational partnership between Justin Greaves and Kemar Roach further frustrated Bangladesh. Their 140-run stand for the eighth wicket propelled the Windies to a commanding total.

The West Indies have declared their first innings after a brilliant batting display, posting a mammoth 450/9 in 144.1 overs at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium. It has been a resolute effort by the hosts, who batted for over four sessions to put themselves in a dominant position.

Eventually, Hasan Mahmud broke the stubborn partnership late in the session, clean-bowling Roach for a well-made 47. However, Greaves continued his fine innings, reaching his maiden Test ton amidst applause from teammates and spectators.

West Indies added 79 runs in 29 overs during the session, with Greaves and Kemar Roach frustrating the Bangladeshi bowlers early on. Bangladesh missed a crucial chance to dismiss Greaves when he edged a delivery from Taskin Ahmed to the keeper, but neither the fielders nor the bowler appealed, letting the opportunity slip.

Despite Bangladesh trying to shake things up with a mix of pace and spin, their efforts didn’t pay off. They also did not use Shoriful Islam as much and may have missed a trick as he has the knack of picking wickets. Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam bowled with control but could not really create any clear-cut chances. Now, whatever total the Windies post, it will present a tough challenge for Bangladesh. They’ll be hoping to wrap things up quickly after Lunch. Join us at 4.40 pm for the action-packed second session!

Hasan Mahmud made an impact straight away, striking in the very first over to dismiss Joshua Da Silva and following it up with Alzarri Joseph’s wicket soon after. This sparked hopes for the visitors to keep the Windies under 300. However, Justin Greaves had other plans. Starting cautiously, he found the occasional boundary to keep the scoreboard moving, with Kemar Roach providing steady support at the other end.

SESSION SUMMARY - 86 runs and 2 wickets in 26 overs! Bangladesh got off to another strong start, much like they did on Day 1. However, they once again struggled to capitalize on the momentum, allowing the hosts to wrest back control. The Windies ended the session on a huge 336/7 with a superb effort from Justin Greaves, remaining unbeaten on 63 and adding crucial 75 runs along with Kemar Roach.

PITCH REPORT! Samuel Badree and Curtly Ambrose analyze the pitch conditions on Day 2, noting its continued seamer-friendly nature. They highlight that Day 1 saw a tricky start, with several edges induced, and expect similar challenges today. On closer inspection, they observe noticeable marks in the good-length area and moisture still present in the surface, contrary to expectations of it drying out. They predict movement for the bowlers, making conditions potentially challenging for the batters once again.

With the first ball of Day 2 just moments away, all eyes will be on Bangladesh’s bowlers to see if they can capitalize on the breakthroughs from yesterday evening. On the other hand, the Windies batters will look to carry their fight forward and set the tone for the day. Stay tuned as another exciting day of Test cricket unfolds!

Despite Louis’s patient 97 from 218 balls and Athanaze’s fluent 90 off 130 deliveries, the final session belonged to Bangladesh. Both batters fell agonizingly short of centuries, providing the visitors with a morale boost as they wrapped up the day on a high note. Joshua de Silva and Justin Greaves held their ground in the closing moments of Day 1, ensuring no further damage was done. They will resume the innings today, with the West Indies aiming to build on their overnight momentum and post a commanding first-innings total.

Winning the toss and choosing to bowl, Bangladesh’s disciplined bowling attack got off to a dream start, reducing the hosts to 25/2 early in the first session. Taskin Ahmed led the charge, claiming the first two wickets and putting the pressure squarely on the Windies batters. However, Mikyle Louis took charge and anchored the innings brilliantly. His partnerships were the highlight of the day, first combining with Kavem Hodge to add 59 runs for the third wicket. Later, he forged a magnificent 140-run stand with Alick Athanaze for the fourth wicket, steering the West Indies past the 200-run mark.

A warm welcome to everyone joining us here today for the start of Day 2 of this first Test match between West Indies and Bangladesh. The hosts managed 250/5 on Day 1 after being asked to bat first by Bangladesh. After an intriguing Day 1, the stage is set for Day 2 of this Test match, with the West Indies looking to capitalize on their strong partnerships and resilience.
... DAY 2, FIRST SESSION ...

Right then, that is it from an entertaining Day 1 of this first Test. West Indies are in a good position with 250/5 on the board, but Bangladesh will be eyeing early inroads and restricting them under 300. We did lose six overs of play but Day 2 is still expected to start at 2 pm GMT, but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

West Indies took control in the final session, with Alick Athanaze's counterattack and Mikyle Louis’s steady hand powering a 100-plus run stand. Both batters stormed into their 90s, but the tension of the nervous nineties struck hard - Louis fell after a shaky patch, and Athanaze followed soon after. Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam’s spin broke the partnership just in time for Bangladesh. Yet, the second new ball backfired, as Joshua Da Silva and Justin Greaves countered with quick runs, steering the Windies safely to stumps. A gripping day ends with the hosts holding the edge and Bangladesh plotting a comeback.

West Indies fought back brilliantly in the afternoon session, closing at 116/3, led by Mikyle Louis’s gritty, unbeaten 71 off 166 balls. With seven boundaries, Louis anchored the innings, fending off a relentless Bangladeshi attack. Kavem Hodge’s run-out for 25 was the only blip, but his partnership with Louis steadied the ship. Alick Athanaze’s composed presence added 32 crucial runs for the fourth wicket. The Bangladeshi pacers were a bit inconsistent, letting the batters take advantage while the spinners Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam probed without any reward.

Opting to bowl first proved a good decision for Bangladesh, with Shoriful Islam and Hasan Mahmud setting the tone early with disciplined spells. Though wickets eluded them initially, Taskin Ahmed broke through with two crucial strikes, dismissing both Kraigg Brathwaite and Keacy Carty. The Windies struggled to keep the scoreboard ticking, but Mikyle Louis showed resilience, finding rhythm as the session progressed, with Kavem Hodge providing steady support. Heading into Lunch, the hosts faced an uphill battle to regain momentum, while Bangladesh were eager to press their advantage and seize control.

SESSION SUMMARY - 134 runs and 2 wickets in 30 overs! Well, a hard-fought day of Test cricket comes to an end! Bangladesh were the ones who took control in the first session with some brilliant pace bowling but the momentum shifted quickly with West Indies coming back hard in the next two sessions. The visitors did manage to get a couple of crucial breakthroughs in the last hour of play, but this game is very much in the balance.

Bangladesh employed five bowlers, with Taskin Ahmed leading the charge, claiming 2/34 with the ball jagging both ways. The West Indies have staged a solid comeback in the afternoon session, finishing at 116/3, thanks to Mikyle Louis’s composed and unbeaten 71 off 166 balls. Kavem Hodge was the only casualty of the session, falling for a hard-fought 25 off 63 deliveries. His dismissal came through a run-out at the striker’s end while attempting a risky second run. However, the fourth-wicket partnership between Louis and Alick Athanaze has added a vital 32 runs, stabilizing the innings.

... DAY 1, SECOND SESSION ...

The West Indies managed to navigate the first hour without significant damage, but their inability to keep the scoreboard moving is something they’ll need to address after Lunch. Braithwaite soaked up plenty of deliveries in an effort to wear down the pacers but eventually fell shortly after the first hour. Carty couldn’t make an impact either. The silver lining for the hosts was Mikyle Louis, who started cautiously but became more proactive once he settled in. Hodge offered solid support, and together they saw out the rest of the session without further setbacks. The Windies will look to build on this partnership and inject some aggression into their innings, while Bangladesh will be eager to strike early in the next session to take control of the game. Join us at 4.40 PM GMT to find out how the second session unfolds!

Opting to bowl first after winning the toss turned out to be a smart decision for the visitors. The pace duo of Shoriful and Hasan Mahmud kept things tight with the new ball, making life tough for the openers, although they couldn’t break through before the drinks break. It was Taskin Ahmed who capitalized on their disciplined efforts, using his clever setups to claim both wickets in this session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 50 runs and 2 wickets in 23 overs! Bangladesh will head into the break feeling slightly more satisfied, though they haven’t pulled too far ahead. The West Indies batters adopted a cautious approach, making run-scoring a challenging task in this session, but they are still very much in this contest.

Commentary.Commentary: Here we go! Bangladesh walks out with the ball in hand to start the Two-match series along with the Umpires to start the Test match. Kraigg Brathwaite, the skipper of the West Indies walks out to open the batting along with Mikyle Louis. The youngster Hasan Mahmud takes the new ball for Bangladesh. Let's Play!

Moments away from the start, the teams and the officials walk out for the National Anthems! Its the National Anthem of Antigua and Barbuda followed by that of Bangladesh and finally the National Anthem of the West Indies.

PITCH REPORT! Curtly Ambrose and Samuel Badree analyze the pitch, noting it appears to be an excellent surface with an even covering of grass. They highlight that the pitch is hard and contains some moisture, which will likely favor the fast bowlers. According to them, the surface offers bounce and lateral movement, promising an engaging contest for the pacers.

Kraigg Brathwaite, the captain of West Indies says that they would have bowled first as well with some moisture on the pitch but it could get hard to bat on later in the game. Adds that the guys have played in the Super50 and they are in good spirits. Mentions that they have had a lot of success with pacers here and that is why they are going with four seamers. Ends by saying that getting to a good start will be crucial and they need to stick to the plans and get those big hundreds.

Mehidy Hasan, the skipper of Bangladesh says that they are looking to use the weather conditions at the start and put some pressure with the new ball. He further mentions that the team has been on a bit of a roller coaster but they are going to start the series with confidence and hopefully things will fall into places for them.

On the other hand, Bangladesh arrived with mixed fortunes of its own. Their historic 2-0 Test series victory against Pakistan was a statement of intent, showing they could punch above their weight against higher-ranked opponents. Yet, subsequent defeats to India and South Africa revealed the gaps in their game. As they gear up for this contest, the visitors will be eager to prove that their recent success wasn’t a one-off and that they can sustain their competitiveness on foreign soil.

For the West Indies, it has been a rocky road since their triumphant Test victory at the Gabba against Australia in January, a match defined by Shamar Joseph’s fiery bowling spell that dismantled the hosts. That moment of brilliance, however, has been followed by a string of forgettable performances. A 3-0 series whitewash at the hands of England, coupled with a challenging tour of South Africa, has left the Caribbean side searching for consistency. Back on home soil, they will look to reignite their spark and rediscover the fighting spirit that once defined West Indies cricket.
